title: Prime Video Sets August 28 Global Launch for Paatal Lok Team’s Babita Singh Reporting
excerpt: Nimisha Sajayan makes her Hindi OTT debut as a police officer whose murder investigation at her in-laws’ home unravels the secrets of her own marriage, in a new crime drama from the creators of Paatal Lok.
body:
• Prime Video has set August 28 as the global launch date for Babita Singh Reporting, an investigative crime drama from the creators of Paatal Lok.
  • The series stars Nimisha Sajayan, celebrated for Malayalam hits like The Great Indian Kitchen, in her Hindi OTT debut as an underestimated police officer investigating a murder at her in-laws' home.
  • Written by Sudip Sharma (NH10, Udta Punjab, Paatal Lok) and directed by Ambika Pandit, the show blends crime investigation with a deeply personal story about duty, family and marriage.
  • The trailer, released on August 17, shows Sajayan's ASI Babita Singh navigating the collision between her professional obligations and the hidden dynamics within her husband's family.

Prime Video has locked August 28 as the global premiere date for Babita Singh Reporting, an investigative crime drama that reunites the creative team behind one of Indian OTT's most acclaimed series.

The trailer, released on August 17, introduces Nimisha Sajayan as ASI Babita Singh, a police officer whose first visit to her in-laws' home collides with a murder investigation. The result is a story that forces its protagonist to juggle two impossible tasks simultaneously: solving a crime and confronting uncomfortable truths about her own marriage.

The Paatal Lok Pedigree

The series comes with serious credentials. Sudip Sharma, who wrote NH10, Udta Punjab and created the critically acclaimed Paatal Lok for Prime Video, serves as executive producer and writer. Saurabh Malhotra, who co-created Paatal Lok, is among the producers alongside Manoj Mittra and Tina Tharwani. The show is directed by Ambika Pandit and produced by Film Squad Productions in association with Act Three.

https://x.com/DEADLINE/status/2089237100713619645

Paatal Lok, which premiered in 2020, remains one of the most talked-about Indian crime series on any streaming platform. Its unflinching portrayal of India's criminal justice system, caste dynamics and media manipulation set a new standard for Indian OTT content. Babita Singh Reporting appears to carry forward that DNA of layered, character-driven crime storytelling, but with a distinctly feminine perspective at its center.

Nimisha Sajayan's Hindi Debut

The casting of Nimisha Sajayan is perhaps the show's most intriguing element. The 30-year-old Kerala-born actor has built a formidable reputation in Malayalam cinema with performances in The Great Indian Kitchen, a searing critique of patriarchal household dynamics, and Auf Wiedersehen Monsoon. She won the Kerala State Film Award for Best Actress at just 22.

Babita Singh Reporting marks her entry into Hindi-language content, and the role — a cop who must maintain professional authority while navigating the social pressures of being a daughter-in-law — plays directly to the kind of nuanced, emotionally complex work that has defined her career.

"When an underestimated cop visits her in-laws' for the first time, she finds herself torn between uncovering the truth in a murder investigation and the hidden lies in her own marriage."

— Official series logline, Prime Video

The Supporting Cast

Joining Sajayan are Barun Sobti, known for television's Iss Pyaar Ko Kya Naam Doon and the digital series Tanhaiyan, in what is described as a pivotal role. Anshuman Pushkar and Sunita Rajwar round out the key cast. The combination of Sajayan's intensity with Sobti's emotional range suggests the series is positioning the personal drama — the marriage, the family secrets — as equal in weight to the criminal investigation.

Global Streaming for Indian Crime Drama

The series will stream on Prime Video across more than 240 countries and territories, continuing the platform's strategy of positioning Indian original content for global audiences. For the Indian diaspora, the show arrives at a moment when Indian crime dramas — from Paatal Lok to Delhi Crime to Kohrra — have built a growing international audience hungry for stories that offer both genre thrills and social commentary.

Babita Singh Reporting was first announced at Prime Video's "It All Starts Here" showcase event on March 19, 2026, alongside an ambitious slate that includes Panchayat Season 5, Farzi Season 2 and The Revolutionaries.

What to Watch For

The August 28 premiere places the series in a competitive window for Indian streaming content. With the Diwali theatrical season approaching and several high-profile releases clustered in the final quarter, Prime Video appears to be banking on the pre-festival period to capture audiences before attention shifts to the big screen. The Paatal Lok team's track record suggests the show will aim for the same blend of pulpy entertainment and pointed social observation that made its predecessor a cultural moment.
